 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 21-7-2022 at about 8.00 p.m. the petitioner was wallking on the foot path on the left side of the road, near Srushti School, Heggadadevanapura road,
Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru, at that time, one motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-EE-4629 ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner came from back side and dashed against the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Abhay Vasishtha Hospital, Madanayakanahalli, Bengaluru wherein she took treatment as an inpatient.
She was discharged with an advise of follow-up treatment and had spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards her medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment.
4. It is stated that, prior to the accident the petitioner hale, healthy and was working as a Tailor and also doing maid servant and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, she could not able to do any work as earlier.
It is stated that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the rider of motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-EE-4629.
In this regard, case was registered against the rider of offending vehicle by the jurisdictional Madanayakanahalli Traffic Police, in Crime No.0344/2022.

As such, the respondent No.1 being the R.C. owner, the respondent No.2 being the policy holder and Parvathi Bai vs Amar.K on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33205918/
2 the respondent No.3 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition,
seeking compensation.
6. In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 & 2 have not appeared before the court, remained absent, hence, placed exparte.
On the other hand, the respondent No.3 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement 7.
In the written statement of the respondent No.3, it is contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

Further it has denied the manner in which the accident took place, injuries sustained, avocation, 5 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 age and income of the petitioner and also expenses incurred towards medication and other incidental charges.
The respondent has admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending vehicle and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
It is the defense of the respondent No.3 that there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-EE-4629.
It is contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner herself.

Further contended that the rider of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident and I.O. has charge sheeted the driver Amar K. u/s 279 and 338 of IPC R/W Section 3(1) R/W Section 181 of IMV Act.
It is also the contention of the respondent No.3 that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant.
Upon these grounds, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in 6 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 a motor vehicle accident which was taken place on 12.7.2022 at about 8.00 p.m. near Srushti School, Heggadadevanapura road, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-  02-EE-4629 in an actionable  negligence?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
3.
What order
or award?
9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, she herself examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to P12.
In addition to her evidence placed the evidence of Dr.S.A.Somashekara as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P13 & Ex.P14.
Further examined MRO of Abhay Vasishtha Hospital as PW3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P15 to Ex.P18.

Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the materials available on record.

12. My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3:

As per final order,
 for the following:
 R E A S O N S ISSUE NO.1:-
13.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02- EE-4629, the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently she had sustained grievous injuries.

14. On the other hand, the respondent No.3, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, seriously disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 & 2 remained absent, placed exparte.
The petitioner in order to prove her case, examined herself as PW1.
PW1 in her examination- in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to P8
. Ex. P1-true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.344/2022 of Madanayakahanalli Traffic Police Station, Ex.P2-true copy of the first information statement given by the petitioner.

Ex.P3-true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P4 & Ex.P5- notice u/s 133 of M.V. Act and reply to notice u/s 133 of MV Act, Ex.P6-true copy of wound certificate of the petitioner, Ex.P7-true copy of IMV report, Ex.P8-true copy of the charge sheet in Crime No.344/2022 of Madanayakanahalli Traffic police.

16. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner, the S.H.O. of Madanayakanahalli Traffic Police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 337 of IPC and section 187 of IMV Act.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the 9 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC and section 181 and 187 of IMV Act.

17. Apart from this, even at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent No.2 about the denial of allegation made against the rider of Parvathi Bai vs Amar.K on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33205918/
4 the offending vehicle.
18. On the contrary, though the respondent No.3 has examined his legal officer as RW1, but his evidence will not much helpful to disprove the case of the petitioner.

19. In the light of the evidence placed on record, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA- 02-EE-4629.
As such, the petitioner has placed the satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.
Hence, without making much discussion on the point of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the issue No.1, in the Affirmative.
10 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 ISSUE NO.2 :
20 . This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

21. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him, in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of 11 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P6.

The said document discloses that, she had sustained the following injuries:-

5 1) Abrasion over the forehead right side temporo 2) Left distal fibula fracture 23.
In connection with the above said injuries, the doctor is of the opinion that the injury No.1 is simple in nature and the injury No.2 is grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summaries per Ex.P9 issued by Abhay Vasishtha Hospital reveals that the petitoner was admitted on 12.7.2022 and discharged on 17.7.2022.
In addition to her evidence, placed the 12 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 evidence of Dr.S.Somashekara as PW2.
PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained post traumatic left distal fibula fracture.
He has placed clinical note and x-ray as per Ex.P13 & Ex.P14.
Apart from their evidence placed the evidence of MRO as PW3.
He has placed authorisation letter, policy intimation, MLCextracta nd case sheet as per Ex.P15 to Ex.P18.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, she could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.25,000/-
under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
24.
PW1 has stated that, she was doing tailoring work and earning 20,000/- per month.

She has not placed any documents to show that she was earning Rs.20,000/-
per month.
In such a situation notational income is apt to be taken applying the same principle like other cases.
On going through the discharge summary issued by Abhay Vasishtha Hospital marked at Ex.P9 the petitioner was 13 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 admitted on 12.7.2022 and discharged on 17.7.2022.
During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to her to do daily routine work at least for a period of one month by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by her.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.15,500/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
25.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of his evidence, placed medical bills of Rs.16,274/- as per Ex.P11 along with prescriptions at Ex.P10.
There are no contra materials available on record to show prove that the medical bills are created and fabricated.

Hence,
it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.16,274/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
26.
The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summaries the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient and also as an outpatient.

During that Parvathi Bai vs Amar.K on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33205918/
6 period, definitely the petitioner could have spent 14 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.

Loss of future income;
27.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, she had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by her.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on her evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.

As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P6 goes to show that, she had sustained grievous injuries for which she took the treatment as an inpatient and also as an outpatient.
To substantiate this, the petitioner had placed discharge summaries for consideration.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.S.A.Somashekara examined as PW2.
PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained Post traumatic left distal fibula fracture.
ORIF with plate and screws for left distal fibula.

He 15 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 has placed clinical note and x-ray as per Ex.P13 &
Ex.P14.
28.
On examination of the petitioner, the petitioner walks with pain and limping, diffuse swelling of left leg and ankle is seen, surgical scars are seen over left leg and ankle.
X-ray shows united fracture distal fibula with implants in situ.
PW2 assessed the disability of left lower limb at 26% and whole body is 13%.
29. At the time of cross-examination of PW2, he admitted that he is not the treated doctor.
Further admitted that the petitioner has sustained only one fracture and the said fracture is united.
This witness also denied the suggestion that, he assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side.

30. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW2 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW2 by following the guidelines issued by Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Government of India and accordingly petitioner has 13% disability of whole body.

entities.text: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability 16 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 expressed by PW2, it is apt to take whole body disability as 10% instead of 13%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
31. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 47 years.
The petitioner in order to prove her age she has relied upon Ex.P12 Aadhar card which shows the date of birth of the petitioner as 5.9.1975.
The accident took place on 12.7.2022.
From this document, it can be said the petitioner was aged about 47 years at the time of accident.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '13' is to be taken into consideration.
32. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in her evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident, she was working as a tailor.

But she has not placed any Parvathi Bai vs Amar.K on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33205918/
7 document to show her income.
In such a situation, as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in 17 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2022.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,500/- for the year 2022.
33. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner

,
definitely come in the way of her future, in a slight manner, to do her daily routine work, as well as to do her work for livelihood on going through her age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.15,500 X 12 X 13 X10/100= Rs.2,41,800/-.
Loss of amenities;
34.
As noted above, the petitioner has sustained fractures in the accident as a result she has permanent partial disability.
The petitioner was aged about 47 years at the time of the accident.

The said disability certainly affects not only on her avocation, but also affects on her amenities as the petitioner could not able to enjoy her life as she was enjoying earlier prior to the accident.
By overall 18 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 considering these aspects it is just and proper to award Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities.
35. In connection with the future medication, PW2 has stated that petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants which would cost of Rs.40,000/-.
But, the cost of estimation was not produced.

However, having considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner and escalation of rates in all the fields even including in medical field, this tribunal is of opinion that, it is proper to award Rs.20,000/- under the head future medical expenses.

36. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
Compensation heads Compensation amount 1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 25,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs. 15,500-00 laid-up period and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs. 16,274-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 6,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 19 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 5.

Loss of future income Rs.2,41,800-00 due to disability Parvathi Bai vs Amar.K on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33205918/
8 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 10,000-00 7.
Future medication Rs. 20,000-00 Total Rs.3,34,574-00 37.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,34,574/- (Rupees three lakhs thirty four thousand five hundred and seventy four only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

LIABILITY:
38.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-EE-4629, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

On the other hand, the respondent No.3- Insurance company in the written statement and in the evidence strongly contended that, as on the date of the accident, the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving license to ride the same.
Thereby violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
As such, insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
To substantiate the same, respondent No.3 has examined Legal Manager as RW1.
He has reiterated the contents as averred in the written statement.

He has placed authorisation letter and policy copy as per Ex.R1 & Ex.R2.
40.

In this regard, on going through the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer, relevant provision has been inserted stating that, at the time of accident the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving license.
To disprove the contents of the charge sheet and to show that, the rider had valid D.L. no supportive evidence is available on record to impeach the recitals of Ex.P8.
Further Ex.P4 is the notice u/s 133 of MV Act issued by the Investigating officer to the owner of the offending vehicle to produce relevant documents.
In 21 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 answer to the Ex.P4, owner of the offending vehicle had given reply as per Ex.P5, wherein he stated that the rider was not possessing driving licence.

41. At this stage it is relevant to rely the following decisions:
1) MFA 6154/2019 between Hemalatha @ Hema @ Hemavathi & Others Vs. Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd., & Another 2) MFA 3297/2019 between Smt.Adilakshmamma & Others Vs. Raju B. & Another Parvathi Bai vs Amar.K on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33205918/

sentences.text:
With due respect, on going through the above said citations, it is observed that "owner of the offending vehicle amounts to fundamental breach of policy condition within the meaning of Section 149(2)
(a)(ii) of the M.V. Act.
Therefore, exonerating the insurer on the ground that there is fundamental breach of policy condition."

43. In the instant case, respondent No.1 being the owner-cum-rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-EE-4629 did not chose to contest the matter and it is evident from the records, especially the reply as per Ex.P5 given by the 22 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 respondent No.1 being the owner-cum-rider was not possessing valid and effective driving licence.
Under such circumstances insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover, where there is a clear breach of policy conditions.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle, cannot escape from his liability to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest at 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation.
The claim against the respondent No.3-Insurance company is deserves to be dismissed.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
44.

In view of my due discussions on point Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act as against the respondent No.1 is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act as against the respondent No.3 is hereby dismissed.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,34,574/- (Rupees three lakhs thirty four thousand five hundred and seventy four only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.

After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any 24 SCCH-18 MVC No.3324/2023 Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.
